target.title: RFC 0019: Managed configuration
target.body:
## Why this RFC exists

Lobster needs to enforce deployment-owned OpenClaw settings while still allowing normal user customization.

Today Lobster handles this outside OpenClaw by baking configuration overlays into the deployment and applying or repairing those values around OpenClaw's ordinary config lifecycle. The immediate example is Control UI allowed origins: Lobster must provide deployment-specific origins without taking ownership of unrelated Control UI settings.

That private overlay machinery has structural costs:

- OpenClaw sees only the resulting document, not which source owns each value.
- Overlay precedence silently replaces conflicts rather than reporting authority violations.
- Lobster must reproduce parts of OpenClaw's config normalization, validation, reload, and persistence behavior.
- User writes can collide with deployment-owned values unless every write path knows about the overlay.
- Upgrades require stale-value cleanup and exact-blob tests to keep generated config synchronized.
- Other hosts would need to build and maintain equivalent private machinery.

We want an official OpenClaw-supported way to express this relationship, rather than continuing to bake host-specific overlays around OpenClaw.

## Proposed direction

Add a generic ordered configuration-authority model to OpenClaw:

- each source supplies a sparse ordinary OpenClaw config document
- source order defines authority from strongest to weakest
- the first declaration of a path controls that path
- later sources may omit or repeat the authored value, but conflicting values are rejected explicitly
- OpenClaw composes the sparse documents, then runs its normal schema, plugin, cross-field, defaulting, and runtime materialization pipeline once
- provenance and source identity remain inspectable
- source access is explicit and independent of layer names
- activation publishes one complete runtime snapshot or rejects the complete candidate

The model is deliberately generic and recursive. Core has no special host, operator, tenant, Lobster, or two-stage behavior.

## Main Lobster case

A read-only deployment source claims:

- gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins

A writable customization source can independently claim:

- gateway.controlUi.enabled
- other ordinary user-controlled settings

OpenClaw composes the sibling values into the same ordinary runtime config consumed today. If customization attempts to replace the deployment-owned origins, OpenClaw returns a structured ControlledByEarlierLayer finding before persistence instead of silently overwriting either source.

The RFC includes the complete Lobster example:

- source documents
- effective runtime output
- path provenance
- rejected-write response
- architecture and recursive-fold diagrams

This lets Lobster delete its post-seed overlay writer and stale-value cleanup once the supported OpenClaw path ships and passes release proof.

## Scope

This PR contains only rfcs/0019-managed-configuration.md.

It defines the architecture and behavioral contract. Exact loading flags, CLI names, mutation integration, and the first bounded comparator set remain implementation decisions.

## Prototype evidence

A separate fork-only OpenClaw prototype exercises the exact-authority slice, ordered source resolution, effective validation, provenance, and atomic publication:

https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/33

The prototype is evidence for the RFC, not an upstream implementation PR.
